library.title: Youth Climbing Coaching Library: Vocabulary and Activities
library.summary: A growing, de-duplicated master list of climbing activities and climbing vocabulary for coaching kids and teens, with how to run each activity, why it works, how to adapt it by age, how to manage its risks, and where it comes from. Every activity and term named in the weekly curricula is listed here by the same name.

callout.text: Climbing is inherently dangerous, so nothing here promises it is risk-free. Entries talk about managing and reducing risk: checking systems, clearing fall zones, spotting to manage risk, and choosing when not to commit to a move.

library.text: Ages use these groups: Parent & Child (ages 2–3), Ages 3–4, Ages 4–6, Ages 6–9, Ages 9–12, Ages 12+ (training) and Ages 14+ (competitive). Month themes are shared across the age groups. Entries marked coaching practice have no published source; they come from common youth-coaching practice.

dedup.title: Normalize the name
dedup.detail: Lowercase it and strip spaces, hyphens and punctuation (“Add-On” and “add on” both become “addon”). Compare against every existing name and every “also called” alias.

dedup.title: Compare the core rule, not the name
dedup.detail: Write the game in one sentence (what the climber does, and what ends a round). If an existing entry has the same core rule, it is a duplicate even with a different name: add the new name to that entry's aliases and add its source.

dedup.title: Variants go inside the parent entry
dedup.detail: A scoring change, a theme, a prop swap or an age tweak (letters for falls, a dice roll, a board version) is a variation of the parent entry, not a new entry. Only a different core rule or a different purpose earns its own entry.

dedup.title: Same name, different game
dedup.detail: If two sources use one name for two different games, give each a descriptive unique name and keep the source's name as an alias with a qualifier.

dedup.title: Cite or mark it
dedup.detail: Every new entry links the page it came from, or is marked coaching practice. Never invent a source.

dedup.title: Use risk language
dedup.detail: Write about managing and reducing risk, never as if any activity were free of risk; keep source titles verbatim.

dedup.title: Update the counts
dedup.detail: Bump the last-updated date. The counts update themselves from the data.

curricula.title: Youth Curricula by Age Group
curricula.summary: A September–June plan for each youth group, built on my month-by-month chart and adapted to each age using the coaching playbook research. Pick a group to see its chart, a week-by-week plan with vocabulary and timed activities, its session plan and its games.
how: Same rhythm throughout: 4 weeks a month, with Dec and Jun as Review & Play in every group.

The week types change with age. Hard Workout (Grade Pushing) only returns at Ages 12+ (training) and Ages 14+ (competitive); younger groups get Brave Steps, Challenge Climb, Personal Best or Project Push instead.
No games that pit climbers against each other. March is a team or family celebration for younger groups and a personal-best block for older ones.
No campus, hangboard or weighted finger training in any group; strength comes from climbing.

Every week has its own plan: the skill and session type, the vocabulary with an age-pitched kid version, and a 5-minute warm-up, skill block, and game timed to the class length. All 40 weeks for all 7 groups (280 plans) use activity and term names exactly as they appear in the Library.
Climbing is inherently dangerous, so the plans talk about managing and avoiding risk (checking systems, clearing fall zones, spotting, choosing when to commit), never about being risk-free.

callout.text: These are the real class lengths: 60 min (Parent & Child (ages 2–3), Ages 3–4, Ages 4–6), 90 min (Ages 6–9) and 120 min (Ages 9–12, Ages 12+ (training), Ages 14+ (competitive)).

curricula.weekIntro: Pick a month and a week. Dec and Jun are Review & Play months: three review weeks that revisit earlier months, then a celebration week. Look up any activity or term by name in the Library for full steps, why it works, variations by age, risk management and sources.

views.name: This week
views.text: One class on a single card: a 5-minute warm-up, the skill block, a game, vocabulary, and a cue for each part. Print it and take it to the wall. The week follows today's date: days 1–7, 8–14, 15–21, and 22 through the end of the month are the four weeks. July and August open on week 1.

views.name: Roadmap
views.text: Ten month stops for the year. Each card shows the theme and a one-line focus. Open a month for its four weeks.

views.name: Months
views.text: One card per month, with the skills, a few vocabulary chips, and the weeks as tabs.

views.name: Ladder
views.text: Each theme is a lane. Read across the year to see how the skills step up, then open any week.

views.name: Table
views.text: The full grid: month, theme, skill progression, and weekly structure, with the week plan underneath.
